question.text: Monochromatic light of frequency 6.0×10<sup>14</sup> Hz is produced by a laser. The power emitted is 2×10<sup>-3</sup> W. The number of photons emitted, on an average, by the source per second is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>15</mn></msup></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> is an integer. Find the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math>?

solution.text:
P=2×10-3 W

Energy of photon,

E=hv

= 6.6×10-34×6×1014 J

Where h being Planck's constant.

Number of photons emitted per second

n=p E

= 2×10-36.6×10-34×6×1014=5×1015
